$comment: Pinned reference measurements for LexiSharp.Eval. Two kinds of assertion live here and they are
regression pins  — the value LexiSharp produces at a fixed configuration. Tight tolerance.
These are the teeth of the net: deterministic, and they catch any change to
scoring, candidate generation, tokenization or metrics.
parity figures   — the independent implementation's number for the same task and index.
A credibility claim with a source, not a guard. |lexisharp - anserini| is
meaningful only where the configuration is genuinely aligned, and the
arguana row is aligned across different BM25 parameters, which is recorded
as such rather than glossed over.
Run --verify-reference to see what moved, then edit expectedNdcg here by hand: --write is
accepted and writes nothing, deliberately. Read the diff before committing it: re-recording is
how a pinned baseline stops catching anything.

regressionPins.note: The default analyzer, no stemming. Kept because every published table in this repository is this row.
Reference analysis. Gain convention linear, which is what the published figures use.
Above the independent reference at its own parameters (0.6789); see the parity table.
Measured on the full 1406-query split. Note what the exclusion is worth here: +0.0012 (0.2852 without). See the note on the arguana parity row for why that is smaller than it looks.

parity.note: The like-for-like comparison is at the reference's own operating point: 0.3215 measured at k1=0.9, b=0.4 with the reference analysis, against 0.3218. The 0.327 above is this library's default k1/b under the reference analysis.
0.6788 measured at k1=0.9, b=0.4 with the reference analysis, against 0.6789 published.

The deficit this row used to record is measured now, and it was a scoring rule rather than a parameter. The library deduplicates query terms before scoring; the reference scores one clause per query-token occurrence, so a term repeated in the query multiplies its weight. On this corpus every test query is a whole ~200-word argument whose content words repeat, and counting them is worth +0.0705 on its own: 0.2197 -> 0.2902 at the reference's own k1=0.9, b=0.4, and 0.4061 at k1=3.0, b=0.75. On NFCorpus and SciFact, whose queries are short, the setting changes nothing to four decimals. THE 0.4061 IS NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE: it is at a k1 the reference does not use, because this corpus' sensitivity to k1 runs opposite to the other two and the parameters cannot be aligned. A like-for-like ArguAna comparison remains unmeasured and would need the k1/b grid this corpus' 1406 long queries make expensive. THE EXCLUSION IS WORTH MUCH LESS THAN IT LOOKS: measured 0.2852 without, 0.2864 with, i.e. +0.0012. An ArguAna query is a whole document, so its own document is a near-duplicate and ranks first, and 1298 of 1406 test queries have a query id that is a document id -- but the relevant document is already inside the top 10 in all 869 cases where it is retrievable at all (median rank 3), and 537 queries have no relevant document in any page, so excluding the self-match promotes the gold document by one rank in 810 queries and the page refills from rank 11, which is almost never the gold document. A +0.095 estimate for that flag was an artifact of dropping the self-document from an already-cut 10-document page, leaving a hole instead of refilling it.
